title: North Carolina's 1st Congressional District Election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for North Carolina's 1st Congressional District is a rematch between Democratic incumbent Don Davis and Republican challenger Laurie Buckhout, who narrowly lost to Davis by about 1.5 points in 2024. The district was redrawn in October 2025 by the Republican-controlled General Assembly, making it more competitive for Republicans, and the Cook Political Report rates it as 'Lean Republican.' Davis, a moderate Democrat and former Air Force officer, is seeking a third term, while Buckhout, a retired Army colonel who served as acting Assistant Secretary of Defense for Cyber Policy under President Trump, has been endorsed by Donald Trump and is backed by national Republican groups. Libertarian candidate Tom Bailey is also on the ballot, having run as a third-party candidate in previous cycles.

polling.pollster: co/efficient for the National Republican Congressional Committee (NRCC)

polling_note: Only one public 2026 general election poll was identified: an NRCC internal poll showing a tied race. No independent or nonpartisan general election polls were found for the 2026 cycle as of mid-2026.

candidates.name: Don Davis
candidates.summary: Don Davis is the Democratic incumbent representing North Carolina's 1st Congressional District, first elected in 2022. A moderate Democrat and former U.S. Air Force captain, he previously served in the North Carolina Senate and as mayor of Snow Hill. Davis is running for re-election on a platform of lowering costs, creating jobs, and delivering for eastern North Carolina.

candidates.summary: Laurie Buckhout is a retired U.S. Army colonel and the Republican nominee for North Carolina's 1st Congressional District. She served as acting Assistant Secretary of Defense for Cyber Policy in the Trump administration in 2025 and previously ran as the Republican nominee in 2024, narrowly losing to Don Davis. candidates.name: Tom Bailey
candidates.summary: Tom Bailey is the Libertarian Party candidate for North Carolina's 1st Congressional District. A retired roofing contractor and Vietnam War veteran, he previously served on the Guilford County Board of Adjustments and was the Libertarian nominee for U.S. Senate in 2004. Bailey advocates for limited government and free-market principles as a standard-bearer for the Libertarian Party.

forecast.rationale: The race is highly uncertain due to very limited polling. The only 2026 general election poll is an NRCC internal survey from late April showing Buckhout and Davis tied at 41-41 — a single partisan poll with limited independent weight. Structural factors are mixed: the district was redrawn in 2025 to favor Republicans, Cook rates it Lean Republican, and Buckhout lost by only ~1.5 points in 2024. However, Davis is a two-term moderate Democratic incumbent who has won the district before, and the Libertarian candidate (Tom Bailey) could slightly affect the margin. With only one partisan poll and divergent structural signals, the race is best characterized as a tossup with a very narrow Republican lean.
